purpose: Silver sulfadiazine is a cream applied directly to the skin to prevent and treat infections in burns, wounds, and skin ulcers. It is most commonly used on second and third degree burns to keep harmful bacteria from growing. It helps protect damaged skin while your body heals.
how_it_works: This cream contains two infection-fighting ingredients — silver and a sulfa antibiotic — that work together to kill a wide range of bacteria and some fungi. The silver releases slowly into the wound and damages the outer walls of germs, stopping them from growing and spreading. Think of it like a protective shield on your skin that fights off infection around the clock.
common_side_effects: You may notice a temporary burning, stinging, or itching feeling right after you apply it. The cream can leave a grayish or dark discoloration on the skin, which is normal and usually goes away. Some people develop a mild skin rash in the treated area.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are allergic to sulfa drugs, as this cream contains a sulfa antibiotic and could cause a reaction. Do not use this cream on newborn babies, premature infants, or during late pregnancy, as it can be harmful to them. If you develop a widespread rash, fever, or signs of a serious allergic reaction, stop using it and contact your doctor right away. Avoid getting this cream in your eyes or mouth.
typical_dosing: Apply a thin layer of cream — about the thickness of a nickel — directly to the cleaned burn or wound area once or twice a day. The wound is usually covered with a dressing after applying the cream. Your doctor or nurse will tell you exactly how often to change the dressing and reapply the cream based on your specific wound.
